caption: Integrate: a phase growing at half a cycle a second and wrapping at 1, scrolling the stripes
why: Moving something steadily means adding a little every frame - the right little for how long the frame took. Integrate does that: give it a rate (units a second) and it grows by exactly that much a second, whatever the frame rate, wrapping back to 0 at the value you set.

Plug a Speed slider into rate and you have a scroll the slider controls, which keeps its place when the slider moves (a Multiply of time would jump). Its neighbours: Time is seconds since the start; Delay builds a loop by hand; Integrate is a smooth, rate-controlled phase.
steps: **rate** is 0.5: the value grows half a unit a second.
**wrap** is 1: at 1 it starts again from 0, so the value is a phase that cycles every two seconds. **reset**, while on, holds it at 0.
`value` is a **Wave**'s phase (x from **Coords** `u`, 3 cycles): the stripes scroll.
The trace shows the phase: a ramp that climbs to 1 and drops back to 0.

try.label: Faster
try.text: rate 2: the phase cycles twice a second - a quick scroll.

try.label: Never wrap
try.text: wrap 0: the value keeps growing - the trace climbs forever (the stripes look the same, as a Wave repeats every 1 anyway).

try.label: Stopped
try.text: reset on: the value is held at 0 and the stripes stop.
